new_findings.title: Hidden A/B chooser intercepts return-focus lookup after a source selection
new_findings.mechanism: A/B buttons receive the same data-bi-focus as the mark. The chooser is inserted before the SVG, and selecting an origin only sets hidden=true while leaving the buttons in the DOM. restoreBiFocus uses the first matching data-bi-focus without visibility checks, so it picks the hidden chooser button, calls focus with no visible focus result, and returns true.
static_reproduction: Render an actual two-origin BI02/BI03 contribution.
Open its chooser and select A or B; keep the current mount for a detail overlay or same-mount return.
Move focus to a visible detail/return control and invoke restoreBiFocus(container, selected).
The first matching element is a button under the hidden fieldset, preceding the visible SVG mark. Focus is not restored to the visible mark, although the helper returns true.
new_findings.impact: Keyboard users lose the advertised return position after an origin is chosen. Cancel/Escape works through its separate direct returnFocus path and does not exercise this case.
new_findings.bounded_fix: Clear chooser contents when hiding after selection, or skip hidden/disconnected focus targets and confirm focus actually moved before reporting success. Preserve selected valueId/reference and cancel behavior.
new_findings.required_discriminant: After choosing each A/B option for zero and nonzero BI02/BI03 rows, move focus elsewhere and call the exported restoreBiFocus on the retained mount; assert the intended visible mark is document.activeElement. Existing focus tests use singular refs and the new origins test only covers cancellation.
new_findings.evidence_class: Static code/DOM reasoning; not an executed browser failure.
